findings.evidence: `rg -n "RepresentsLaplace\.congr|EqOn.*RepresentsLaplace|RepresentsLaplace.*EqOn" code/TauCeti/Analysis/CompletelyMonotone mathlib/Mathlib` returns no hits, while `LaplaceRepresentation.lean:577-598` shows the predicate and only its finiteness/value eliminators.
findings.fix: Add a public namespace lemma, e.g. `lemma congr (hμ : RepresentsLaplace f μ) (h : EqOn g f (Ici 0)) : RepresentsLaplace g μ`, proved without requiring users to unfold the predicate.
findings.issue: `RepresentsLaplace` only constrains `f` on `[0, ∞)`, but there is no public `RepresentsLaplace.congr`/`EqOn` lemma to transport a representation to another function with the same nonnegative values.

findings.evidence: `BernsteinTheorem.lean:7-9` has `public import TauCeti.Analysis.CompletelyMonotone.BernsteinMeasures`, `public import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.TightNormed`, and `public import TauCeti.MeasureTheory.Measure.Prokhorov`, but the public declarations at `:689-708` mention only `IsClosedCompletelyMonotone`, `Measure ℝ≥0`, and `RepresentsLaplace`.
findings.fix: Make proof-only dependencies ordinary `import`s and publicly import only the modules needed to state the exported theorem, such as the Laplace representation/basic predicate API.
findings.issue: `BernsteinTheorem` publicly imports implementation infrastructure (`BernsteinMeasures`, `TightNormed`, `Prokhorov`), so importing the headline theorem also re-exports proof-only Chafaï/Prokhorov APIs as part of the public surface.

summary: The Laplace algebra API was added, but the representation predicate still lacks a key congruence principle, and the theorem module publicly re-exports proof infrastructure that is not part of the theorem interface.
